section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Average Speed Paradox
section_1.content: Define average rate of change as the slope of the secant line over an interval. Use a visual of a cheetah chasing prey to show that 'average speed' hides the dramatic sprints and pauses during the hunt.
section_1.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed is 20m/s, but at exactly 2 seconds, was it accelerating or slowing down?

section_2.title: The Limit Approach: From Secant to Tangent
section_2.content: Introduce the visual 'shrinking interval' animation. As the two points on the curve get infinitely close (Δt → 0), the secant line morphs into a tangent line at a single point.
section_2.example: An animation showing two points on a parabolic curve moving toward each other until they overlap, visually transforming the chord into a tangent line.

section_3.title: Defining the Derivative
section_3.content: Introduce the formal definition: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Explain this as the 'instantaneous speed' or the slope of the tangent line at exactly point x.
section_3.example: Graph of y = x²; show the slope calculation at x=2 transitioning from a secant slope of 5 to the tangent slope of 4.

section_4.title: Application: The Robot's Velocity
section_4.content: Demonstrate the utility of the derivative. If a cleaning robot's position is a function of time, the derivative allows us to know its exact velocity at any micro-second, preventing it from bumping into walls.
section_4.example: A smart robot's position function p(t) = 3t²; calculating p'(t) = 6t to find the robot's exact velocity at t=3 seconds.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap: Derivative = Slope of tangent line = Instantaneous rate of change. Emphasize that while average change looks at the 'big picture,' the derivative provides the 'precise focus' needed for physics and engineering.
section_5.example: A 10-second summary animation showing a car speedometer needle moving in sync with the calculated derivative of its position function.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Average Speed Paradox", [

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
